name: MCS (Megawatt Charging System)
description: DC-only megawatt charging interface for heavy-duty and other large vehicles, developed by CharIN and specified by IEC TS 63379 (configuration HH, up to 1500 V DC and 3000 A) and SAE J3271. It uses thermal sensing or thermal management of the contacts, single-pair Ethernet (10BASE-T1S) and ISO 15118-20 for charging communication, and an electrically actuated lock.

standards.title: Vehicle connector, vehicle inlet and cable assembly for megawatt DC charging
standards.scope: Configuration HH (Annex A, vehicle coupler 1500 V DC and up to 3000 A); read with IEC 62196-1:2022 and IEC 62196-3:2022. Configuration JJ (Annex B, up to 1600 A) is a different coupler, not modelled here.

standards.title: SAE Megawatt Charging System for Electric Vehicles
standards.scope: Information report covering the coupler, communication and controls, cables and cooling, use cases and interoperability testing.

standards.title: Electric vehicle conductive charging system – Part 23-3: DC electric vehicle supply equipment for megawatt charging systems
standards.scope: Supply equipment the IEC TS 63379 accessories are used with

variants.name: MCS vehicle inlet
mechanicalNotes: The DC contacts of the configuration HH inlet are pins: IEC TS 63379 Annex C specifies DC pins for the vehicle inlet reference device.
The retaining means (electrically actuated lock) is integrated into the inlet side, at one to three locations (CharIN white paper 2.0).
Temperature sensing is required for the DC contacts of both the inlet and the connector.

variants.name: MCS vehicle connector
mechanicalNotes: Tethered to the charger; the cable assembly may use thermal transport (active cooling) and thermal sensing.
The PE contact is 8 mm in diameter (CharIN white paper 2.0).

electricalProfiles.name: DC
conditions: Upper limits of the scope of IEC TS 63379:2026 and of configuration HH: rated operating voltage up to 1500 V DC, rated current up to and including 3000 A, with thermal sensing, or thermal transport and thermal sensing.
CharIN recommends a system operating range of 400 to 1250 V DC for MCS supply equipment and vehicles; the connector itself is designed for 1500 V DC.
The maximum continuous rating has been tested up to 3000 A DC (CharIN white paper 2.0); active cooling is recommended for higher currents.
Configuration HH has inlet reference devices for 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500 and 3000 A (IEC TS 63379 Annex C).
Charging communication uses 10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet on dedicated contacts and ISO 15118-20 only (CharIN recommendation).

ocpi-2.3.0.note: Added in OCPI 2.3.0; OCPI 2.2.1 has no MCS value.

notes: The contact set and contact functions are not recorded: IEC TS 63379 Table 2 (interface overview) and the standard sheets were not reviewed. Secondary sources describe seven contacts (DC+, DC−, PE and four signal or communication contacts) without a primary confirmation of their names.
Contact genders are inferred from the IEC TS 63379 table of contents (DC pins in the configuration HH vehicle inlet reference device); the genders of the signal and PE contacts are not confirmed.

Configuration HH is taken as the CharIN MCS because it matches the 3000 A rating of the CharIN white paper; no source reviewed states the correspondence explicitly. Configuration JJ (up to 1600 A, contact tubes on the inlet) is not modelled.
No face is drawn: no source depicting the mating faces was reviewed.
Open Charge Map has no MCS connection type in the pinned reference data.
The OpenStreetMap socket key for MCS could not be checked against the pinned wiki revision; the mapping is left empty pending that check, not because no key exists.
The EVicons plug-mcs icon (0.8.0) is not attached: no source depicting the MCS mating faces was reviewed.
